question: Walking at (3)/(4) th of his normal speed from his home, Abhishek is 5 minutes late in reaching his office. The usual time taken by him to cover the distance between his home and his office is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio = 3/4 ⇒ Time ratio = 4/3

Extra time = (4/3 − 1) = 1/3 of usual time

⇒ (1/3) of usual time = 5 min

⇒ Usual time = 5 × 3 = 15 min

**∴ Answer = 15 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

New speed = (3/4) of normal speed

Extra time = 5 minutes

**Formula used:**

Time ∝ 1/Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let usual time = t

⇒ New time = t × (4/3)

⇒ Extra time = t × (4/3 − 1)

⇒ t × (1/3) = 5

⇒ t = 5 × 3 = 15 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 15 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relation

Time ∝ 1/Speed for fixed distance

Ratio Trick

If speed becomes a/b, time becomes b/a

Extra Time

Extra time = New time − Original time

Quick Tip

Use fractional difference directly to find original time
